quizName: DMV Practice Test #11 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What is it called when you shift to a lower gear?
questions.correctAnswerText: Engine braking.
questions.explanation: Shifting to a lower gear slows your motorcycle like using the brakes. This is why downshifting is called engine braking.

questions.question: How should your following distance at night compare to your following distance during the day?

options.text: Keep a longer distance at night.
Keep a shorter distance at night.
Keep the same distance day and night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a longer distance at night.
questions.explanation: At night, it is harder to judge distances because you cannot see shadows and light contrasts. Keep a longer following distance when riding at night than during the day.

questions.question: When should you wear reflective clothing?
questions.correctAnswerText: Day and night.
questions.explanation: Bright and reflective clothing helps you be seen in all conditions. Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day, so wear bright clothing at all times.

questions.question: In group riding, what does this hand signal mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: Hand signals are important for group riding. When the lead rider extends their left arm straight down with palm back, all riders should stop.

questions.question: What is an advantage of keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles?

options.text: You can pass danger more quickly.
You have a narrower view so you stay more focused.
You have more time to react to other drivers' movements.
You can more easily follow the next vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: You have more time to react to other drivers' movements.
questions.explanation: Space between you and other vehicles gives you a clearer view of hazards, more time to react, and more room to steer around dangers.

questions.question: What formation should a group use when entering a curve?
questions.correctAnswerText: Single-file formation.
questions.explanation: Use a staggered formation normally, but switch to single-file when turning, taking curves, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: What should you do to lower your chances of a crash?

options.text: Follow the vehicle ahead as closely as possible.
Focus only on your controls and not the road ahead.
Tell other drivers what you plan to do.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell other drivers what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: Reduce crash risk by being visible to others. Use your signals, brake light, and lane position to show your intentions. Keep space around your motorcycle and watch the road ahead, behind, and beside you.

questions.question: How many alcoholic drinks affect a rider's ability to ride safely?
questions.correctAnswerText: One
questions.explanation: Even one drink can affect your riding ability. Riding while under the influence of alcohol is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: What should you do if you can't avoid a slippery surface?

options.text: Speed up and lean the motorcycle.
Speed up and keep the motorcycle upright.
Slow down and lean the motorcycle.
Slow down and keep the motorcycle upright.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and keep the motorcycle upright.
questions.explanation: If you cannot avoid a slippery surface, keep your motorcycle upright and go slowly across it.

questions.question: Is the front brake safe to use?

options.text: Only if the rear brake fails.
No, do not use it regularly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, if used properly.
questions.explanation: The front brake is safe when used correctly. It is more powerful than the rear brake and provides at least three-fourths of your total stopping power.

questions.question: The center of a lane often has an oily strip. This area is:

options.text: Usually safe, unless the road is wet.
Usually safe, unless it is sunny.
Always safe, no matter the weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually safe, unless the road is wet.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars collects in a strip in the center of the lane. When the road is dry, this area has enough grip for motorcyclists. The strip is usually about two feet wide, so you can ride around it while still staying in the center lane.

questions.question: If another driver is following too closely, you should:

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to get them in front of you. If it is safe, change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up may only make them tailgate at a higher speed.

questions.question: When turning on a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Look at the front of the motorcycle.
Look through the turn to where you want to go.
Turn your entire body to see the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look through the turn to where you want to go.
questions.explanation: Look through the turn toward where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while riding, you should:

options.text: Use both brakes and stop quickly.
Shift your weight toward the good tire.
Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
questions.explanation: Hold the handgrips firmly and keep the motorcycle straight. Ease off the throttle. If you need to brake, slowly apply the brake to the tire that is not flat. As you slow down, move to the side of the road, squeeze the clutch, and stop.

questions.question: To avoid serious injury in a crash, do all of the following except:
questions.correctAnswerText: Have a windshield.
questions.explanation: Reduce your risk of injury by wearing an approved helmet, face or eye protection, and protective clothing.

questions.question: The effects of marijuana can last for:
questions.correctAnswerText: More than six hours.
questions.explanation: When smoked, marijuana affects you within minutes and lasts two to four hours. When eaten, it takes over one hour to start working, but effects can last more than six hours.

questions.question: The front brake:

options.text: Should only be used for quick stops.
Should only be used on slippery roads.
Is not as effective as the rear brake.
Is safe to use when used properly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is safe to use when used properly.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes whenever you slow down or stop. The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake and is safe to use if you use it correctly.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing you, you should:

options.text: Slow down as you approach it, then speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down as you approach it, then speed up.
questions.explanation: Dogs often chase motorcycles. If a dog is chasing you, downshift and slow down as you approach it. Then speed up and leave it behind.

questions.question: Passengers should:

options.text: Sit as far back as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean when the rider leans.
questions.explanation: Passengers should sit directly behind the rider and lean when the rider leans. Sit as far forward as possible without crowding the rider. Hold onto the rider's waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: To best control a motorcycle, a rider should:

options.text: Use arms to hold up their body.
Keep knees away from the gas tank.
Keep feet firmly on the footrests.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep feet firmly on the footrests.
questions.explanation: Sit so you can use your arms to control the motorcycle, not to hold yourself up. Your arms should be slightly bent on the handgrips. Keep your knees against the gas tank and your feet firmly on the footrests to maintain balance.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT required for effective eye or face shield protection?

options.text: It must be too tight to wear sunglasses or eyeglasses.
It must be free of scratches.
It must allow clear views to both sides.

questions.correctAnswerText: It must be too tight to wear sunglasses or eyeglasses.
questions.explanation: Good eye or face shield protection must be free of scratches, fasten securely, allow clear views to both sides, allow air to pass through to prevent fogging, and have room for eyeglasses or sunglasses if needed.

questions.question: How can a motorcycle rider stop other drivers from sharing the lane?

options.text: By giving dirty looks to other drivers
By riding in the center of the lane
By riding on the left side of the lane
By riding in a zigzag pattern

questions.correctAnswerText: By riding in the center of the lane
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane to remove large spaces on either side of your motorcycle. This makes it harder for other drivers to try to share the lane with you.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: When you can see through the vehicle in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the roadway is wet.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when your motorcycle needs more time to stop. You should also increase it in heavy traffic or when you cannot see through the vehicle ahead.

questions.question: What should you do at a blind intersection with a stop sign?

options.text: Stop at the stop sign and proceed through the intersection.
Ignore the stop sign and move forward to see better.
Stop at the stop sign, then move forward slowly to see cross traffic better.
Proceed through the intersection without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop at the stop sign, then move forward slowly to see cross traffic better.
questions.explanation: Stop at the stop sign first. Then move forward slowly and stop again just before the crossroad. Lean forward and look around buildings, parked cars, or bushes to check for traffic. Keep your front wheel out of the crossroad while looking.

questions.question: When do most motorcycle crashes happen?

options.text: After riding for at least an hour.
After riding for more than 8 hours.

questions.correctAnswerText: On short trips.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen on trips shorter than five miles, just a few minutes after the rider starts.
